chunks: And from him (Al-Haytham) from Al-Haytham from Isma'il ibn Sahl from Hammad from Hariz from Al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked, 'For whom is the Fitrah (alms of fasting) permissible?' He said, 'For him who does not find (enough to pay it). And for whom it is permissible, it is not obligatory upon him.'

I said to him, 'Is there Zakat upon the one who accepts Zakat?' He said, 'As for the one who accepts Zakat of wealth, then upon him is the Zakat of Fitrah, and he is not obligated (to pay Fitrah) for what he accepted. And there is no Fitrah upon the one who accepts Fitrah.'

key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat: Alms-tax, a mandatory charitable contribution in Islam.
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah: Alms given at the end of Ramadan, a specific form of charity.
key_terms.زَكَاةَ الْمَال: Zakat of wealth: Zakat paid on accumulated assets/wealth.
key_terms.لَا يَجِد: La yajidu: One who lacks sufficient means or surplus wealth.

ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to pay Fitrah and does accepting Zakat exempt one from it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mutual exclusivity of Zakat and Fitrah, establishing that receiving Zakat on wealth exempts one from the obligation of Fitrah, while receiving Fitrah exempts one from paying it again. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that these two forms of almsgiving serve different purposes and cannot be double-counted for the same individual, ensuring equitable distribution of resources. The narration underscores the principle that eligibility for receiving one form of charity precludes the obligation to pay the other, reflecting a nuanced understanding of financial purity in Shia fiqh.
